subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS Dashboard embedded browser ever receive native device/operator tokens, or must browser injection be limited to configured shared token/password auth?
rationale: The linked bugfix and the sibling parity PR intentionally choose opposite credential boundaries, and removing native-token fallback changes existing upgrade behavior for users without shared Dashboard auth configured.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
options.body: Proceed with this PR's security boundary, update the endpoint reload path, close or redirect the native-token parity sibling, and require proof for shared token plus no-token/password fallback behavior.

options.title: Preserve native-token parity
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction, with explicit security review for injecting native/operator tokens into the browser context.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in mode
options.body: Keep the compatible default and add a documented, maintainer-approved strict shared-token mode only if maintainers want a migration path instead of an immediate behavior change.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR's security boundary, update the endpoint reload path, close or redirect the native-token parity sibling, and require proof for shared token plus no-token/password fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the original native Dashboard/auth helper and the recent endpoint-observer change that defines the current affected surface.
